venues.name: Knoch Park

venues.name: Naperville Jaycee Playground

venues.name: Winding Creek Park

venues.name: Gartner Park
venues.hours: 6 AM–9 PM daily

venues.name: 95th Street Community Plaza & Splash Pad

venues.name: Prairie Point Splash Park

venues.name: DuPage Children's Museum

venues.name: Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park
venues.hours: Mon–Thu 4–8 PM, Fri 4–9 PM, Sat 10 AM–9 PM, Sun 12–8 PM

venues.cost: ~$25/person all-day pass (~$12.50 for 40" & under); $4 socks required

venues.name: Naperville Public Library – Nichols Library
venues.hours: Mon–Fri 9 AM–9 PM, Sat 9 AM–5 PM, Sun 1–9 PM

venues.name: Naperville Public Library – 95th Street Library
venues.hours: Mon–Fri 9 AM–9 PM, Sat 9 AM–5 PM, Sun 1–9 PM
venues.note: Attached to a playground and splash pad — read, then run it off outside.

venues.name: Naperville Public Library – Naper Blvd. Library
venues.hours: Mon–Fri 9 AM–9 PM, Sat 9 AM–5 PM, Sun 1–5 PM
venues.note: Quieter kids' area and easier parking than the downtown branch.

venues.name: Blackberry Farm
venues.hours: Fri 9:30 AM–3:30 PM, Sat 9:30 AM–5 PM, Sun 11 AM–5 PM (seasonal, closed Mon–Thu)
venues.note: Historic farm: ponies, train, carousel, petting zoo. Great for toddlers.

venues.name: Knoch Knolls Nature Center
venues.hours: Mon–Fri 9 AM–4:30 PM, Sat 9 AM–3 PM, Sun closed
venues.note: Paved trails, an aquarium inside, and a disc golf course.

venues.name: Cosley Zoo
venues.hours: 9 AM–5 PM daily
venues.note: Small, affordable zoo (~$8 admission), well suited to toddlers.
venues.cost: Free for kids 11 & under and Wheaton residents; $12 non-resident adults ($10 seniors)

venues.name: Lucky Strike Naperville
venues.hours: 4 PM–12 AM weekdays, later Fri/Sat, 11 AM Sat/Sun
venues.note: Bowling plus arcade; bumper lanes available for little bowlers.
venues.cost: Paid — pay-per-game bowling + arcade, varies by time
venues.age: All ages (bumpers/ramps for little bowlers; some evenings go 21+)

venues.name: Main Event Warrenville
venues.hours: 11 AM–12 AM weekdays, later Fri/Sat
venues.note: Bowling, ropes course, arcade, laser tag — good for birthday parties.
venues.age: 6+ for laser tag & ropes course (height minimums apply); bowling/arcade fine for all ages

venues.name: Round1 Bowling & Arcade – Aurora
venues.address: 2480 Fox Valley Center Dr B13, Aurora, IL 60504
venues.hours: 10 AM–2 AM daily
venues.note: Bowling, arcade, karaoke — gutter guards available for kids.
venues.cost: Paid — pay-per-game bowling + arcade credits, varies by time
venues.age: 8+ — reviewers say it skews toward older kids/teens; loud, two-floor arcade

venues.name: McDowell Grove Forest Preserve
venues.hours: 7 AM–8 PM daily
venues.note: Trails along the DuPage River; some sections are stroller-friendly.
venues.age: All ages — flat trail, paved/stroller-friendly sections

venues.name: Danada Forest Preserve
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Wide gravel trails and an equestrian center; deer sightings are common.
venues.age: All ages for trails & barn visits; formal riding lessons require 12+

venues.name: Springbrook Prairie
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: A 6-mile crushed-limestone loop — good for a jogging stroller.
venues.age: All ages, best for biking or strollers — full loop is 5–6 miles with little shade

venues.name: Riverview Farmstead Preserve
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Small and quiet, with a paved trail and a kayak launch.
venues.age: All ages — short paved trail, easy with a stroller

venues.name: The Fun Playce
venues.hours: Mon closed, Tue–Fri 9:30 AM–5 PM, Sat–Sun 10 AM–6 PM
venues.note: Indoor climbing structure, fenced-in toddler area, and pretend-play corner; built for kids 7 and under.
venues.cost: $18/child open play ($10 on Tuesdays), adults free; 10-visit pass $150

venues.name: Playroom Cafe Naperville
venues.hours: Mon–Thu 9:30 AM–6 PM, Fri 9:30 AM–5 PM, Sat–Sun 10 AM–4 PM
venues.note: Montessori-inspired indoor playground for the 0–6 set, with a real cafe (coffee, smoothies, kid meals) for parents.
venues.cost: $17/child; adults free Mon–Thu, and on Fri–Sun two adults are free per paying child ($17 for extra adults)

venues.name: Kids Empire North Aurora
venues.address: 1610 Orchard Gateway Blvd, North Aurora, IL 60542
venues.hours: Mon–Thu 10 AM–8 PM, Fri–Sun 10 AM–10 PM
venues.note: Large chain indoor playground — arcade, ball pits, slides; all-day admission with re-entry.
venues.cost: $22.90/child (ages 1–17) all-day, 2 adults free per child ($5 each extra); infants under 1 free
venues.age: 1–12 (admits up to 17, but play structures suit younger kids best)

venues.name: Kids Empire Bolingbrook
venues.hours: Mon–Thu 10 AM–8 PM, Fri–Sun 10 AM–10 PM
venues.note: Same chain-playground formula as the North Aurora location — arcade, ball pits, slides, all-day admission.
venues.cost: $22.90/child (ages 1–17) all-day, 2 adults free per child ($5 each extra); infants under 1 free
venues.age: 1–12 (admits up to 17, but play structures suit younger kids best)

venues.name: Hyper Kidz Wheaton

venues.note: Unlimited-time indoor play with no session limit; weekday pricing is noticeably cheaper than weekends.

venues.name: Hyper Kidz Bolingbrook
venues.hours: Mon–Fri 9 AM–8 PM, Sat 9 AM–9 PM, Sun 9 AM–8 PM
venues.note: Sister location to Hyper Kidz Wheaton — same unlimited-time play model, socks required.
venues.cost: Weekday $9.99–14.99/child by age, weekend $14.99–19.99/child; 2 adults free per paid child

venues.name: Ball Factory
venues.hours: Mon–Tue 9:30 AM–3 PM, Wed closed, Thu 9:30 AM–7 PM, Fri 9:30 AM–6 PM, Sat–Sun 10 AM–6 PM
venues.note: Four-level indoor play structure with a dedicated toddler zone and a full Italian-style cafe on site.
venues.cost: Check website — sold as day passes/multi-visit passes, not posted per-visit; siblings under 1 free

venues.name: TreeTop Escape

venues.note: Indoor rainforest-themed climbing structure inside the West Chicago Park District's ARC Center, with tube slides up three levels; cash/on-site only.
venues.cost: $10/child (1–12), one free adult per paying child

venues.name: Red Oak Nature Center
venues.address: 930 N River Rd, North Aurora, IL 60542
venues.hours: Mon–Fri 9 AM–4:30 PM, Sat–Sun 10 AM–3 PM
venues.note: Small nature center on the Fox River with wood-chip trails and a limestone-fireplace picnic shelter.

venues.name: Hidden Oaks Nature Center
venues.hours: Wed–Sun 10 AM–4 PM, Mon–Tue closed
venues.note: Forest Preserve District of Will County nature center with prairie/forest/savanna trails and fishing access.

venues.name: Hickory Knolls Discovery Center
venues.address: 3795 Campton Hills Dr, St. Charles, IL 60175
venues.hours: Building Mon–Sat 10 AM–4 PM (Sun closed); grounds open daily dawn–dusk
venues.note: St. Charles Park District nature center with live-animal exhibits and 3+ miles of trails through oak woodlands.

venues.name: Springbrook Nature Center
venues.hours: Grounds open daily dawn–dusk; visitor center hours vary by season — check website
venues.note: Itasca Park District nature center with 2 miles of trails (partly paved), an aquarium, and a bird mews.

venues.name: Brookfield Zoo
venues.hours: Mon–Fri 10 AM–5 PM, Sat–Sun 10 AM–6 PM
venues.note: Major zoo (216 acres) with both indoor habitats like Tropic World and outdoor exhibits; stroller/wagon rentals available.
venues.cost: $29.95 adult, $20.95 child (3–11), free 2 and under; parking $17 (North Gate) / $20 (South Gate)

venues.name: Morton Arboretum
venues.hours: Daily 7 AM–sunset (Visitor Center and Children's Garden 10 AM–5 PM)
venues.note: 1,700-acre arboretum with miles of tree collections and trails; the 4-acre Children's Garden is the main draw for kids.
venues.cost: Check website — dynamic day-by-day pricing (roughly $20s/adult), $2 more at the gate than online; free for kids 3 and under
venues.age: All ages (Children's Garden best for young kids)

venues.name: Wil-O-Way Commons Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Playground and open riverside green space right on the DuPage River Trail, with kayak/paddle access to the river.
venues.age: All ages — playground plus a flat riverside trail

venues.name: Frontier Sports Complex
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Large sports complex behind Neuqua Valley HS with a renovated central playground, skate park, and pond, alongside ball fields, courts, and picnic shelters.
venues.age: All ages — playground for younger kids, skate park and ball fields for older kids

venues.name: Wil-O-Way Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Small neighborhood park next to Wil-O-Way Commons with a playground, baseball backstop, and basketball courts.

venues.name: Central Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Downtown playground (slides, swings, a bucket-levee sandbox) next to the Community Concert Center bandshell.
venues.age: All ages — slides and swings for younger and older kids, sandbox for toddlers

venues.name: Country Lakes Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Inclusive playground (renovated 2017) designed for kids of all abilities, plus a sled hill and multi-use trails.

venues.name: Burlington Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Quiet wooded preserve with footpaths along the West Branch DuPage River; no playground, good for a short nature walk.
venues.age: All ages — quiet nature walk, no playground equipment

venues.name: St. James Farm Forest Preserve
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Historic McCormick horse farm with scenic trails, sculpture-dotted grounds, and a public indoor riding arena.
venues.cost: Free (arena riding $10/rider-horse if you bring your own horse)
venues.age: All ages for trails; arena riding is age 12+ (under 18 must ride with an adult)

venues.name: Greene Valley Forest Preserve
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: 13.8 miles of trails and a 190-ft scenic overlook with Chicago skyline views, open weekends May–October.
venues.age: All ages — best for older kids/bikers on the longer trails

venues.name: Waterfall Glen Forest Preserve
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: 9.5-mile crushed-limestone perimeter loop popular with cyclists and joggers, with a small man-made waterfall (Rocky Glen) built by the CCC in the 1930s.
venues.age: All ages — best for older kids/cyclists on the long perimeter loop

venues.name: Warrenville Grove
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Riverside woodland preserve along the West Branch DuPage River with picnic areas and a trail past a small dam.
venues.age: All ages — flat, short trail good for young kids

venues.name: Goodrich Woods
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily

venues.age: All ages — short (0.5 mi) easy loop, good for young kids

venues.name: Centennial Beach

venues.cost: $8–17/person, age & residency-based (youth 3–17: $8 resident/$15 nonresident; adult: $10/$17; discounted $5/$9 after 5 PM)

venues.name: Naper Settlement

venues.cost: $6 adults (13+), $5 seniors (62+), $4 youth (4–12); free for Naperville residents and members
venues.age: 4–12, though younger kids can tag along

venues.name: Cantigny Park

venues.note: Sprawling former estate with formal gardens, a large playground, and an outdoor tank park at the First Division military museum.
venues.cost: Museum & garden admission free; parking $5/car ($10 weekends & holidays May–Sep), free the first Wednesday of each month

venues.hours: Mon–Fri 9 AM–5 PM, Sat–Sun 9 AM–6 PM (seasonal variation — check website)

venues.cost: Chicago residents $19.95 adult general admission; non-residents from $38.95 adult / $28.95 child (under 3 free); total-experience passes cost more

venues.name: Field Museum

venues.hours: 9 AM–5 PM daily (last entry 4 PM); closed Thanksgiving & Christmas

venues.cost: ~$30 adult / ~$21 Chicago resident general admission, discounted child pricing; free for IL residents select Wednesdays

venues.name: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
venues.address: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637
venues.hours: 9:30 AM–4 PM daily; closed Thanksgiving & Christmas
venues.note: Huge hands-on science museum — real U-505 submarine, coal mine, and dome theater. Formerly "Museum of Science and Industry"; still commonly called MSI.
venues.cost: $25.95 adult / $14.95 child (3–11); Chicago residents get $9/$5 off; free for Illinois residents select days

venues.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
venues.hours: 10 AM–5 PM daily (grounds open earlier/later seasonally)

venues.name: Chicago Children's Museum
venues.hours: Mon, Wed, Thu 10 AM–2 PM; Fri–Sun 10 AM–5 PM; closed Tue
